why: The defect this issue actually shipped before a browser caught it: a start builds the session, the canvas, the world and the seed, and then leaves the player on the Main Menu with the match running invisibly behind it. Pressing Continue appears to do nothing. WHY EVERY UNIT ASSERTION MISSED IT is the reason this entry is worth its slot -- the whole suite counted what was BUILT (one session, one canvas, one world, the right intent) and every count was correct. Nothing asked whether the thing built was ever SHOWN. `tools/visual/roundtrip.mjs` reported `canvases: 1` with the title buttons still on screen, and a follow-up probe found the pause panel unreachable because the machine had never left the menu. The cases that kill it read `enteredIds`, a ledger BY SESSION ID rather than a count: a boundary that revealed the first handle every time would report the same total as one that advances, which is the same stale-capture shape the disposal ledger beside it exists to catch. 2 of 58 in the scoped run: the single-start case and the repeated-start ledger. The third case in that group -- "reveals nothing when the capability probe refused the start" -- asserts an EMPTY ledger and so keeps passing, which is what makes the trio a real two-way discrimination rather than three restatements of one fact.
